name: Romaine Lettuce
notes:
Romaine lettuce, nutrition from USDA. 96% is edible. World yield ~25 t/ha (FAO, all lettuce; FAOSTAT pools lettuce with chicory); US romaine ~34.9 t/ha (USDA, 2022–2024).

This entry used to be a single 'Lettuce' entry (all types). It was split into romaine and iceberg; the nutrition in it was already USDA's romaine record. Water, emissions, pesticides, fertilizer and tillage are not type-specific, so both entries share the same lettuce-wide values: water is 130 L/kg from the Water Footprint Network's online calculator (Mekonnen & Hoekstra's own figure is 237; the US value, 113, is their US average), and emissions use Poore & Nemecek's 'Other Vegetables' (0.5–0.53).

Pesticides (~1.4 kg/ha) are from USDA surveys of California and Arizona. Lettuce is grown in several short crops a year, so the field is tilled ~3 times a year. Availability is the world lettuce-and-chicory total, shared by both entries.
land_types_note: Irrigated California/Arizona and Mediterranean Spain, plus temperate China and Europe.

Omega-3 from FDC 169247 per 100 g: ALA 0.113 g (USDA's total 18:3, which is almost all ALA), EPA + DHA 0 mg (EPA 0 + DHA 0); divided by 100 for per-gram values.

source.title: Mekonnen & Hoekstra — Water Footprint of Crops (Report 47)
source.note: Romaine lettuce — water_per_kg: 130 L/kg used (sourced from WFN online crop database). Report 47 Table A1 reports 237 L/kg. The discrepancy reflects different methodologies: Report 47 uses a global production-weighted virtual water model; the WFN online calculator (130 L/kg) applies simplified blue+green accounting. Neither is clearly wrong; the lower figure may reflect the dominant role of intensive irrigation-efficient greenhouse production (particularly in China). Value flagged but not corrected — difference is within methodological range.

name: Spinach
notes:
Spinach, nutrition from USDA. Yield is ~20 t/ha (FAO). China grows about 90% of the world's spinach. Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (305 L/kg). Emissions: Poore & Nemecek's value (0.47) and 'Other Vegetables' (0.53).

Spinach is grown in several short crops a year, each with seedbed preparation (~3 tillage passes). Pesticides (~0.6 kg/ha) and fertilizer (~120 kg/ha) are generic leafy-vegetable estimates; the pesticide total has no recorded derivation.
land_types_note: Irrigated California/Arizona and Mediterranean Spain, plus temperate China and Europe.

name: Kale
notes:
Kale, nutrition from USDA. FAO doesn't report kale separately (it's pooled with other brassicas), so yield (~15 t/ha) is an estimate from broccoli and cabbage yields (confidence 3). Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (237 L/kg). Emissions use Poore & Nemecek's brassica values (0.49–0.51).

Availability is weak: there's no world kale statistic, so it uses only US harvested area (2022 Census) × this yield ≈ 110 Gg (confidence 1). Real world supply is far larger (Europe, East Africa's sukuma wiki, Brazil's couve). Kale is therefore penalised on availability more than it should be.
land_types_note: Temperate Europe/US Northeast plus irrigated California.

name: Cabbage
notes:
Cabbage, nutrition from USDA. 80% is edible (outer leaves and core removed). China grows about half the world's cabbage. Yield is FAOSTAT: ~30.6 t/ha world, ~45.1 t/ha US.

Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (280 L/kg). Emissions use Poore & Nemecek's 'Brassicas' (0.51 kg CO2e/kg). Pesticide and fertilizer rates come from USDA vegetable surveys (2020–2022; ~5.6 kg/ha pesticide, ~141 kg/ha fertilizer) and stand in for the world.
land_types_note: China grows about half the world's cabbage; India, Russia, Korea, Ukraine and Eastern Europe make up most of the rest.
